items.name: block-typography
items.title: Slide typography
items.description: Two primitives every other block builds on. Eyebrow is an uppercase accent label at --slide-label-size with --slide-label-tracking letter spacing, in --primary. SlideHeading is an h1 at --slide-heading-size capped at max-w-5xl with an optional lead paragraph at --slide-lead-size in --muted-foreground. Both read the theme's size tokens rather than Tailwind text sizes, so they resize when you retune the type scale. Add this if you are writing your own slide layouts and want the deck's heading rhythm without copying class strings. Every other Deckard block depends on it.

items.name: block-slide-layouts
items.title: Slide layouts
items.description: The five whole-slide frames a deck reaches for most. HeroSlide centers an opener at half again the --slide-title-size, because a theme sizes a title for a slide that also carries copy and an opener carries nothing else. BreakerSlide is the same eyebrow and title rhythm at the plain token size, left-aligned and vertically centered, for a section divider. ContentSlideCard puts an eyebrow, heading, and lead above a bordered --slide-surface panel, and is for body content with no surface of its own. OpenContentSlide is the same intro with no panel, for content that brings its own frame: a FeatureGrid, a BulletList, a chart. FocusSlide is the slide that is one block and nothing else, a code sample or a list or an image with no heading around it: it hands the block the whole frame at the normal type scale, so a code sample shows more lines rather than bigger ones, and takes one optional kicker string. All five pull the title from useSlideTitle() when you do not pass one, so a slide's title stays defined in one place. They respect --slide-content-gap, --slide-radius-lg, --slide-surface, --slide-surface-border, and --slide-surface-shadow, which means a theme swap restyles them with no edits.

items.name: block-collections
items.title: Slide collections
items.description: Two ways to put a list on a slide without it turning into a wall of bullets. BulletList numbers each item 01, 02, 03 in a left rail and rules the rows off with a bottom border, at --slide-body-size on a 64ch measure, so the line length holds when a FocusSlide swaps the body size up. FeatureGrid lays three cards across on --slide-surface-muted, each with a title and a supporting paragraph at --slide-support-size. Both carry data-slide-surface, which is what makes a ContentSlideCard around them warn rather than quietly frame a frame; compose them through OpenContentSlide or FocusSlide instead. Both are presentational and take plain arrays, so a server component can await the data and pass it straight in. Use BulletList for four to six sequential points and FeatureGrid for three parallel ones. Neither scrolls, so trim the copy instead of adding a seventh item.

items.name: block-media
items.title: Slide media
items.description: Photo and video slides that fill the 1920x1080 canvas properly. FullscreenMediaSlide bleeds an image or a video to every edge and lays optional copy over the bottom on one of three scrims, from --slide-media-overlay-subtle to -strong; the framed variant insets it in a bordered surface instead. ImageShowcaseSlide splits the canvas 1.2fr to 0.8fr, image left and a caption panel right. Both take next/image sources, forward blurDataURL from a static import when the source carries one, take unoptimized so an SVG served from public/ skips the image optimizer instead of needing dangerouslyAllowSVG, and use SlideMediaVideo from @deckard/core so video pauses on slides the audience is not looking at. Both pad against --slide-chrome-top and --slide-chrome-bottom, so the deck header and slide counter never sit on top of a caption. Use these instead of dropping an img on a slide, which will not fit the canvas and will not respect the chrome.

items.name: block-metrics
items.title: Slide metrics
items.description: One export, StatGrid, for the three-figures slide every deck reaches for once. It takes exactly three stats, typed as a tuple so a fourth is a compile error, and marks them up as a description list. Each column is a figure at --slide-title-size in --slide-font-heading with an optional unit at --slide-subheading-size, a caption at --slide-support-size capped to 24 characters a line, and a 2px rule across the top in --slide-surface-border. It sets no color of its own, so the rule picks up the theme border weight, and it carries data-slide-surface so a panel around it says it is framing a frame. In a FocusSlide three numbers carry the whole canvas with nothing else around them. A figure is not a heading element, so it carries data-stat-value for themes that treat headings as more than a font: nexus and ledger style it, the other four leave the figure as the block sets it. Take the caption seriously. A number on a slide without the thing it is measured against is decoration, and the 24ch measure is sized for "up from 2.6k", not for a sentence.

items.name: preset-blocks
items.title: Deckard blocks
items.description: Every slide block in one add, plus the one stylesheet line a consumer cannot guess: the @import of @deckard/core/styles.css, which carries the slide token contract and registers the package's own Tailwind source so the runtime classes survive tree shaking. Use this once, right after installing @deckard/core, then write slides. The theme is not in here and does not need to be: the six Deckard themes are named exports of @deckard/themes, so a deck picks one with an import rather than an install.
items.docs: The blocks land in app/slides/blocks/, and the stylesheet import above is the whole build wiring. @deckard/core ships compiled and its stylesheet registers its own Tailwind source, so there is no transpilePackages entry and no @source line for you to add. What is left is deck code: create deck/deck.ts, import a theme from @deckard/themes, pass it to defineDeck, then render the deck from app/slides/[id]/page.tsx with createSlideRoute from @deckard/core/next. Run deckard eject theme when you want that theme as three files in deck/theme/ you can edit.
